heuristics: H1: the class-level r-adding walk with 2^16 adders behaves as a random mapping on the (r-1)/2 negation classes, up to an exponent penalty of at most 4/2^16.
H2: fruitless 2-cycles occur at rate at most 2^-16 per step and 3..64-cycles at rate at most 2^-32 per step.
H3: Callgrind instruction counts on 2^18 sampled P-256 walk steps on each of two input sets represent per-step work; all instructions are charged, 830 per step against 817.6 measured.
limitations: H1 is an unproved standard heuristic; it is tested only on toy curves with up to about 2^33 classes.
The model success bound is 0.411523 at tau = 0.5303, 0.0215 above 0.39; pooled toy-curve success at that budget is in the evidence.
Analytic production cost; no production-size execution.
Needs about 2^68.5 stored distinguished points; not a practical attack.
